title: Second InterAI Workshop: Human-Centred Embodiment at HRI 2026
excerpt: Di Fu and fellow organisers brought together the HRI community for the second InterAI Workshop, with discussions of embodiment, responsible robotics and flexible human-robot teaming.
content:
Had a great time at the Human-Robot Interaction Conference! Yesterday, we successfully organised the 2nd InterAI Workshop. This year, we focused on embodiment in HRI and what it means to design truly human-centric robotics. Beyond improving efficiency in human-robot collaboration, it is equally important to ensure these systems are developed responsibly.

Many thanks to all our speakers and participants. We really appreciated the thoughtful and engaging discussions throughout the workshop.

A special thank you to our two keynote speakers:
Prof Ginevra Castellano (Uppsala University), who presented 'From Human-like to Human-Centric Robots: What Type of Alignment to Humans Do We Need?' Her talk offered valuable insights into how robots should embody human qualities, particularly when interacting with vulnerable groups such as children and women in the perinatal period, and highlighted the importance of ethical AI governance.

Dr Michael Hagenow (University of Wisconsin-Madison), who presented 'Toward Flexible & Effective Human-Robot Teaming.' He introduced approaches for learning from demonstrations and designing versatile interaction interfaces.
